summary: What I like about AgentMemoryRepo is that it reduces cross-session agent memory to a git repo of markdown with `[[wiki]]`-style cross-links, so the whole thing stays greppable, diffable, and inspectable without pulling in a vector store or an opaque embedding pipeline. The "Dreaming" consolidation pass—merging duplicates, resolving contradictions, spotting patterns across sessions—is the kind of background toil-removal that makes a multi-session workflow actually sustainable, and it maps cleanly onto PenguPool, where I already route parallel agent sessions that need to share findings without stepping on each other. It's still a spec rather than a shipped implementation, but the composability model (clone a second user's memory repo into the same machine, track who said what, write back to the right repo) is exactly the primitive I'd want under AgentOn Pocket once a session outlives a single phone interaction.
